item.title: It Was Just An Accident | Arthouse Now — Fri Oct 16, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Mechanic Vahid is jarringly reminded of his time in an Iranian prison for being branded a "dissident" when he has a chance encounter with Eghbal, a man he strongly suspects to be his sadistic jailhouse captor. Panicked, Vahid rounds up some of his fellow ex-prisoners to try and confirm Eghbal's identity and determine what to do next. Panahi creates a deeply felt moral thriller, combining high stakes tension with unexpected humor and thoughtful, yet devastating, questions regarding persecution and revenge. [103 min; thriller, drama; Persian with English subtitles]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Tale Blazing by MDWST Fable — Fri Oct 16, 7:00 PM — The Hundredth Hill
item.description:
Join us for this year's edition of Tale Blazing, when you'll hear five stories around five fires in the nighttime woods
MDWST Fable and The Hundredth Hill present an evening of storytelling in an atmosphere as old as humanity: around a crackling fire in the dark woods. Designed to shift our listening and change our approach to stories, Tale Blazing will bring together five unconventional storytellers exploring what it means to keep our light shining, even when all seems dark. Listen to tales, wander together, and then end the night with friendship and snacks.
Learn more and buy tickets here https://www.eventbrite.com/e/tale-blazing-an-evening-of-fireside-storytelling-tickets-1996466367649 .
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Oct 17 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Oct 17 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Oct 17 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Neighbors Helping Neighbors — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM — Banneker Community Center
item.description:
Neighbors Helping Neighbors is a quarterly event that gives community members a chance to trade goods and access free services. Attendees are encouraged to bring plants, seeds, books, games, or similar items to trade, but even if you have nothing to bring, you can still go home with a new treasure.
The theme for this event is "Health." Health resources will include flu shots, a pharmacist available to discuss medication questions, blood pressure checks, a healthcare navigator, and tai chi and qi gong demonstrations, along with other local organizations that provide healthcare services.
Source: BloomingtonOnline Events

item.title: BYOB(Bring Your Own Business) Dunn Meadow Event — Sun Oct 18, 12:00 PM — Dunn Meadow 1 (West side and concrete pad)
item.description:
Calling all savvy shoppers and student vendors! BYOB @ IU welcomes all students to showcase their businesses at our bi-weekly events, currently held at Dunn Meadow. While sellers must be IU students, our events are open to the wider Bloomington community. You’ll find a diverse range of student-run businesses offering everything from vintage clothing and jewelry to art prints, plants, and crochet items. Set up your table, set your prices, and engage with various shoppers. Our events highlight the creativity and entrepreneurial spirit of our members while providing invaluable real-world experience in marketing, negotiating, and customer interaction. BYOB @ IU is more than just an organization—it's a movement dedicated to empowering the next generation of entrepreneurs, helping them bring their ideas to life and connect with a broader audience.
Hosted by: Bring Your Own Business
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12898427

item.title: Batting Around the World, 1922: Hoosiers in Japan — Tue Oct 20, 12:30 PM — Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies
item.description:
Early in 1922, the Indiana University Baseball team received an invitation from Waseda University professor Iso Abe (Abe Isoo, aka "Father of Japanese baseball") to travel to Japan to play a series against both Waseda and Keio Universities. Abe believed that building these sorts of relationships would lead to a more harmonious world and had begun organizing baseball exchanges in 1905. Please stop by this pop-up event to learn more!
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries, IU Hamilton Lugar School

item.title: Asian Cultures Around Campus: Mahjong Meetups — Wed Oct 21, 4:00 PM — Asian Culture Center (807 E 10th street
item.description:
Once associated with older generations, Mahjong has now found a new home among the young. Social clubs have emerged dedicated to playing Mahjong to reconnect with culture and, more importantly, to foster new friendships. At the ACC, we offer a casual and informal Mahjong experience, perfect for those looking to learn the game, take a break from the digital world, and most importantly, meet new friends in person. You do not need to be an expert to join us, just bring your enthusiasm and a willingness to learn!
All Indiana University events, groups, activities, and educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all IU students and other members of the Indiana University community.
Hosted by: Asian Culture Center
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12898210
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs

item.title: Embedded Accessible Educational Services (AES) — Fri Oct 23, 8:00 AM — LGBTQ+ CULTURE CENTER
item.description:
At the LGBTQ+ Culture Center, we want every student to have the resources they need to thrive. Disabilities come in all shapes and sizes, and many are not visible to others. Accessible Educational Services (AES) partners with students to provide accommodations, support services, and tools that help create equal access and opportunity at IU. item.description:

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Oct 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Oct 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Oct 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: A Well-Advised Lunch with Lisa Hasson — Wed Oct 28, 12:00 PM — MERRILL HALL (MUSIC) / MUSIC
item.description:
Hasson currently serves as Chorus Master and Apprentice Artist Program Director at Des Moines Metro Opera, as well as an opera faculty member at the Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music. Praised for her opera chorus direction, coaching, and administrative expertise, Hasson brings a unique perspective on building and sustaining a career in the classical music industry. Students will gain practical insight into making themselves more competitive for opera chorus opportunities, strengthening their résumés, navigating the transition from a master's degree into the profession, and maintaining an active opera career while balancing supplemental income. Whether you're preparing for auditions, looking to workshop your résumé, or wondering how to build a sustainable career after graduation, this riveting conversation is not to be missed!

item.title: AMP Bloomington 2026 — Wed Oct 28, 2:00 PM
item.description:
AMP Bloomington is a three-day, Homecoming-week event that brings Bloomington’s founders, investors, employers, students, university leaders, and community partners into the same rooms on purpose, so everyone building the city can connect in one place.
Day 1 opens at the Buskirk-Chumley Theater with a keynote from Sweetwater CEO Mike Clem on growing a national retailer from Indiana. Featured speakers include Brian Kelsey of Heartland Forward, Katherine Pease of Pathstone, Polina Osherov of Pattern, and IU faculty Tatiana Kolovou, Isak Nti Asare, and David Wild, with more still to be announced.
When you register, tell organizers who you want to meet, so you leave with a real next step. Attendance is free and includes a coworking day pass at The Mill, and students are especially encouraged to come.
Learn more and register at: https://amplifybloomington.org/amp-bloomington/ https://amplifybloomington.org/amp-bloomington/
Source: Buskirk-Chumley Theater, Pillar Arts Community Calendar,

Accessible Educational Services (AES) partners with students to provide accommodations, support services, and tools that help create equal access and opportunity at IU. Kade Padgett, M.A., an AES Access Coordinator, is available at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center every Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. during drop-in advising hours. Whether you're curious about accommodations, have questions about the process, or simply want to learn more about available resources, we invite you to stop by and chat with Kade about the support options that may be available to you. All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all members of the Indiana University community.
Source: IU LGBTQ+ Culture Center

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Fri Oct 30, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour — Fri Oct 30, 1:00 PM — Lilly Library
item.description:
Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library — Fri Oct 30, 2:00 PM — Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.)
item.description:
You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) and The Signers (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/the-signers). Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries
